wiktionary.gloss: The member of staff at a restaurant who keeps the wine cellar and advises the guests on a choice of wines; a wine steward / stewardess, a wine waiter / waitress / server.

blocks.etymology: Borrowed from French sommelier (“originally, a person in charge of the beasts of burden carrying wine”), from somme (“pack”) + -ier (suffix forming the names of jobs). somme is from Vulgar Latin *sauma, from Latin sagma (“packsaddle”).

wiktionary.gloss: To act as a sommelier.

tastelessness by virtue of being cheap and vulgar

thesaurus.definition: seize and take control without authority and possibly with force; take as one's right or possession
take on titles, offices, duties, responsibilities
free someone temporarily from his or her obligations
take on as one's own the expenses or debts of another person
take over ownership of; of corporations and companies
do over

wiktionary.gloss: To assume control of something, such as a business or enterprise, and sometimes by force.

examples: He will take over the job permanently when the accountant retires.
wiktionary.gloss: To adopt a further responsibility or duty.

examples: My husband is taking over the accounts department during the holiday period, while the chief accountant is away.
If you will take over driving, I'd like to get some sleep.
wiktionary.gloss: To relieve someone temporarily.

examples: Acme Motors is to take Jetcar Industries over this week, if all goes as planned.
wiktionary.gloss: To buy out the ownership of a business.
To appropriate something without permission.

examples: Ancient Rome took over lands throughout the known world.
wiktionary.gloss: To annex a territory by conquest or invasion; to conquer.

examples: Buzz Lightyear has taken over Woody as the most popular children's toy.
Tiger Woods has taken over as the top golfer.
wiktionary.gloss: To become more successful than (someone or something else).

examples: He took the car over to the garage.
wiktionary.gloss: Used other than figuratively or idiomatically: see take, over.

examples: "This weather sucks." "That's right."
wiktionary.gloss: Synonym of indeed, indicating agreement with another speaker's previous statement.

examples: "So you only want the salmon?" "That's right."
wiktionary.gloss: Synonym of right, indicating confirmation.
There is a bad person in any group.

blocks.etymology: Blend of three + even (“divisible by two”). Earliest known usage is from 2006 (see quotes).
vi_block: (toán học, không trang trọng) Chia hết cho ba.

examples: Twenty-seven is a threeven number.
wiktionary.gloss: Divisible by three.

blocks.etymology: Borrowed from Scots tot, a shortened form of totum (“small child; tot”), of uncertain origin, perhaps shortened from totter (“to move in an unsteady way”), Compare tottle, also Old Norse tottr (“name of a dwarf”), Swedish tutte (“small child”), Danish tommeltot (“little child”).

senses.definition: a very young child who has just learned to walk

examples.en: The nursery is full of cheerful tots playing with toys.
examples.vi: Nhà trẻ đầy những đứa trẻ nhỏ vui tươi đang chơi đồ chơi.

senses.definition: a small amount of a strong alcoholic drink

examples.en: He enjoyed a warm tot of rum before going to bed.
examples.vi: Ông ấy thưởng thức một hớp rượu rum ấm trước khi đi ngủ.

senses.definition: the final number obtained after adding several figures together

examples.en: Check your tot to make sure no numbers were missed.
examples.vi: Hãy kiểm tra lại tổng cộng để đảm bảo không sót số nào.

thesaurus.definition: a small amount (especially of a drink)
a young child who is just beginning to walk

examples: He learned to run when he was just a tot.
wiktionary.gloss: A small child.
A small amount of liquor, (particularly) a small measure of rum.
A small cup, usually made of tin.
A total, an addition of a long column of figures.

blocks.etymology: Clipping of total (“to sum”).

senses.definition: to add numbers together to find the final total

examples.en: She quickly totted up the weekly expenses on her phone.
examples.vi: Cô ấy nhanh chóng cộng các khoản chi tiêu hàng tuần trên điện thoại.

thesaurus.definition: determine the sum of

wiktionary.gloss: To sum or total.

examples: a totted debt
wiktionary.gloss: To mark (a debt) with the word tot (Latin for "so much"), indicating that it was good or collectible for the amount specified.

idioms.gloss: Immature; childish; having attributes of children's play.

phrasal_verbs.gloss: To calculate the sum of a number of numbers or quantities.

blocks.etymology: From Middle French votif, from Latin vōtīvus (“votive”), from vōtum (“vow”).

examples: She placed a votive offering at the shrine.

examples: The church was lit by votive candles.
wiktionary.gloss: Of, expressing, or symbolizing a vow. Often used to describe thick cylindrical candles found in many churches, lit when making a private vow or asking a private intention.
